title: Choose the visual world
question: Bolder hand. The deal led with The Calavera Broadside. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Calavera Broadside
options.lineage: Mexican penny-press broadsides with relief-engraved calaveras
options.thesis: One endless printed sheet where engraved skeletons act out the descent, summit to core.
options.viewport: A wood-type headline over an engraved band: a skeleton mountaineer on Everest, gasping on a third of the air, facts in two hard columns below.
options.risk: Dense two-column text can slow a 2–5 minute visit, and every engraving must be hand-authored line art.

raised.raise: Quiz moments: a figure like the inner-core temperature waits behind a REVEAL you press before it inks in.
Any gap in the sourced outline prints as a blank, uninked block, never as invented text.
The plate collision is one pull: drag and the flat ocean floor gathers into the folded Himalaya.

options.label: The Copy-Shop Zine
options.lineage: photocopied zines on coloured copier stock
options.thesis: Each layer is a new sheet of coloured copier paper; the deeper you go, the more the copies degrade.
options.viewport: A lunar-blue sheet, one typed column, the heading SUMMIT enlarged until its letters break and run off the edge.
options.case: Wins both axes: students know photocopied handouts by heart, and one typed column on one colour per layer reads instantly; copy degradation honestly shows deeper numbers are estimates.
options.risk: Lo-fi on purpose; set timidly it reads as a messy handout rather than a made thing.

options.label: Risograph Strata
options.thesis: Earth's layers as cut-paper spot-ink shapes that overprint and misregister as you scroll.
options.viewport: Everest cut from federal blue over pink, inks a hair out of register, a third colour blooming where they overlap.
options.case: Holds clarity (stacked ink shapes read as strata) but students identify with it less than the leader's skeletons.
options.risk: A popular designer look; three inks can't colour-code six layers without overlaps doing the work.

options.label: Teletext Pages
options.thesis: Pages 100–600, one per layer, keyed by number.
options.case: Declined: these students never met teletext, and paging breaks the continuous descent.
options.kept: REVEAL: hidden answers wait for a press.

options.label: Azulejo Hall
options.thesis: The descent painted in cobalt tile panels.
options.viewport: A cobalt Everest panel across the tile seams.
options.case: Declined: cobalt-only can't carry the rising heat, and tiles aren't geology's world.
options.kept: Missing content shows as a blank tile, not a guess.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull turns a flat plane into volume.
options.viewport: A flat black semicircle and one gold cord.
options.case: Declined: fashion has no claim on the Earth's interior.
options.kept: One pull gathers flat crust into folded mountains.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The classic 'journey to the center' scroll story, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A night-sky Everest silhouette, a big title, and a depth meter pinned to the side.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every Earth-layers explainer on the web.
